_meta.what: Follow-the-money: land-value capture in Kolkata, anchored on New Town / Rajarhat, the township WBHIDCO assembled by acquiring ~7,500+ acres of farmland. The atlas's strongest Kolkata DOCUMENTED-FACT anchor is the CAG commercial audit of HIDCO (revenue forgone via discounted/quota allotments) — Tier-A. The coercive land-acquisition politics (CPI(M)- then TMC-era violence) and the 'syndicate raj' are Tier-B reported allegations, with denials noted. This is Ghosh's colonial 'recoupment' running in its home city: the Calcutta Improvement Trust (1911) reborn as WBHIDCO/KMDA.

tier_legend.B: reported allegation (attributed; denial noted where available)

_meta.authoritative_sources: CAG commercial audit of WBHIDCO (Report for year ended Mar 2009, tabled W.B. Assembly); West Bengal government inquiry into New Town land distribution (2017); established press (Business Standard, The Statesman, The Caravan, Scroll, ThePrint, Mainstream Weekly, Sanhati). Allotment-loss figures are CAG's own audited numbers.

actors.actor: WBHIDCO (West Bengal Housing Infrastructure Development Corporation)
actors.role: State development corporation (1999); the land-assembly and allotment body for New Town, Rajarhat — successor in logic to the Calcutta Improvement Trust (1911) and parallel to KMDA
actors.how_they_profit: The recoupment machine: acquires ~7,500+ acres of farmland cheaply under public-purpose powers, services it, then allots/sells serviced plots — but the CAG finds the public uplift was systematically given away through discounted and quota allotments rather than captured for the exchequer.
actors.mechanism: land-value capture via development authority; discounted/quota allotment
actors.project: New Town / Rajarhat township (acquisition begun 1999; central business district + IT parks)
actors.claim: DOCUMENTED FACT (AUDITED): The CAG commercial audit of HIDCO (report for the year ended Mar 2009) detailed procedural violations across the allotment process and put the total quantifiable loss at about Rs 788 crore — including a revenue loss of Rs 371.75 crore from bulk allotment of 508.79 acres to 55 firms; Rs 179.47 crore from selling to 8,573 allottees below the stipulated price; and a separate Rs 124.87 crore loss on land allotted to Tata Consultancy Services in violation of financial propriety. The audit also recorded that by Mar 2007 HIDCO had rehabilitated only ~17% of ousted families despite beginning acquisition in 1999.
actors.source: CAG commercial audit, WBHIDCO, year ended Mar 2009; Business Standard 'Rajarhat allotments come out of closet' (22 Feb 2010) and 'Tata Housing under CAG cloud' (16 Feb 2010); Mainstream Weekly 'West Bengal: Land, Money and the Marxists in New Town.'
actors.denial_if_any: HIDCO and the then Left Front government defended quota/discounted allotments as policy instruments to attract IT/anchor investment; the audit treats the forgone revenue itself as the finding. TCS's allotment was defended as a legitimate investment incentive.

actors.role: Discretionary allotment of New Town plots outside open process via 'chairman's quota' and 'special quota'
actors.how_they_profit: Discretionary quotas confer prime serviced plots on chosen recipients below market/stipulated price — the discretionary capture point where allotment becomes patronage.
actors.project: New Town / Rajarhat plot allotments (chairman's quota, special quota)
actors.claim: DOCUMENTED FACT (AUDITED): The CAG identified the use of 'chairman's quota' and 'special quota' as among the most glaring violations of procedure and financial propriety in HIDCO's plot allotments, contributing to the quantified loss. A separate West Bengal government inquiry (2017) was ordered into alleged irregularities in New Town land distribution.
actors.source: CAG commercial audit (year ended Mar 2009); The Statesman 'Inquiry to probe alleged irregularities in land distribution in New Town' (2017); Mainstream Weekly.
actors.denial_if_any: Officials characterised discretionary quotas as standard administrative allotment categories; the audit treats their use to allot below stipulated price as the irregularity.

actors.actor: State land acquisition for Rajarhat (CPI(M)-era; named leaders incl. Gautam Deb)
actors.role: Compulsory acquisition of farmland from ~Rajarhat mouzas for the township, under the Left Front government (Housing Minister Gautam Deb's portfolio)
actors.how_they_profit: Acquisition at farm-gate compensation, far below the serviced-plot value the township would command, is the coercive 'cheap-in' end of the value-capture spread; farmers allege gunpoint coercion and inadequate compensation.
actors.mechanism: land-value capture via development authority; coercive land assembly
actors.project: Rajarhat land acquisition (~7,500 acres; mouzas across Rajarhat-Gopalpur)
actors.claim: REPORTED ALLEGATION: Affected farmers, organised as the Rajarhat Krishi Roksha Committee (Save Rajarhat Farmers' Committee), allege that during acquisition CPI(M) cadres forced people to accept acquisition notices 'at gunpoint' and that compensation and rehabilitation were grossly inadequate (CAG-confirmed ~17% rehabilitation by 2007). The committee remained non-party; some members say Mamata Banerjee declined support unless they identified with the TMC.
actors.source: Sanhati 'A history of the brutal Rajarhat land acquisition' (excerpted); The Caravan reporting on Bengal land agitation; Mainstream Weekly.
actors.denial_if_any: Left Front leaders (e.g. Gautam Deb) defended the acquisition as lawful public-purpose township development and disputed the coercion characterisation; no criminal adjudication of the named leaders for the acquisition itself. Compensation/process disputes, not convictions.

actors.role: Local 'syndicates' originally formed of land-losers to supply construction material to New Town builders; later alleged extortion networks controlling materials supply
actors.how_they_profit: Syndicates allegedly compel promoters/contractors to buy construction material (often inferior) at inflated prices, skimming a levy off every project in the township — a private tax on the building boom the public land assembly created.
actors.mechanism: contractor-politician nexus; extraction from the building boom
actors.claim: REPORTED ALLEGATION: Syndicates began ~1995 as the CPM government encouraged displaced land-losers to supply construction material; reporting describes their metamorphosis into organised extortion rackets forcing builders to buy materials at high prices. By 2011 (when TMC first took power) the TMC reportedly controlled 175 Rajarhat syndicates and the CPI(M) 215. In 2016 West Bengal Police reported arresting 9,000+ people in connection with real-estate syndicates.
actors.source: ThePrint 'What is Bengal's syndicate raj' (611146); HuffPost 'Bengal's Syndicate Raj: A Left Legacy That TMC Has Inherited'; Scroll 'WB Police arrest more than 9,000 in connection with real estate syndicates.'
actors.denial_if_any: Both major parties deny institutional sponsorship of syndicate extortion, attributing it to the other and to local 'anti-socials'; the phenomenon is widely reported but individual culpability is largely unadjudicated. Treated here strictly as reported allegation.

actors.actor: KMDA (Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority) + Salt Lake / New Town real estate
actors.role: Metropolitan planning/development authority (1970, ex-CMPO); holder and developer of metropolitan land including the Salt Lake (Bidhannagar) and New Town real-estate belt
actors.how_they_profit: The improvement-trust function at metropolitan scale: KMDA-planned, state-assembled land in Salt Lake and New Town becomes a high-value IT/commercial real-estate market, with the uplift captured at allotment and onward sale rather than by the elected corporation.
actors.mechanism: land-value capture via development authority; SPV/IT-corridor real estate
actors.project: Salt Lake (Bidhannagar) Sector V IT hub; New Town real-estate belt; KMDA metropolitan landbank
actors.claim: ANALYSIS: KMDA and WBHIDCO together hold and monetise the metropolitan land that the elected Kolkata Municipal Corporation does not — the structural 'recoupment' pattern Ghosh traces from the 1911 Calcutta Improvement Trust. Salt Lake's Sector V (the IT hub) and New Town are the modern face: public land assembly, public servicing, and a private real-estate market whose appreciation accrues outside the elected body. The metro here is run by Indian Railways (not a state real-estate SPV), so the real-estate-capture vector is the development authorities, not the metro.
actors.source: Analytical synthesis tying the Calcutta Improvement Trust (docs/the-corporate-city.md; Ghosh) to KMDA/WBHIDCO; service_providers.json (KMDA as state board; Kolkata metro run by Indian Railways).
